bit.name: evaluate at every field element by multiplying each term by a fixed power
bit.mechanism: to find where a polynomial vanishes over a finite field, keep one register per coefficient; moving from one element to the next multiplies each register by a fixed power of the generator, so every evaluation costs one multiply per term and a sum, and a zero sum marks a root
requires: a finite field with a known generator
fails_when: linear in the field size; useless over large fields

bit.name: sift elements through a stabiliser chain, adding whatever does not sift to the identity
bit.mechanism: fix a sequence of points; at each level keep one representative for every place the level's point can be sent; to sift an element, at each level compose with the inverse of the representative that undoes its action on that point; an element that sifts to the identity is already generated, otherwise its residue is added as a new generator and the affected levels are re-closed
requires: a permutation action
a base of points (policy)
fails_when: a poor base makes the chain long

bit.name: define new cosets on demand and merge them whenever a relation forces a coincidence
bit.mechanism: keep a table of how each generator moves each known coset; whenever tracing a relation needs an undefined entry, define a new coset; whenever tracing shows two coset names must be equal, merge them (and everything that follows from the merge); stop when every relation closes on every coset
requires: a finite index (otherwise it never stops)
fails_when: no bound on the intermediate table size; infinite index never terminates

bit.name: add the reduced combination of each pair until every pair reduces to zero
bit.mechanism: for every pair in the current set, form the combination that cancels their leading terms, reduce it by the whole set, and if anything remains add it as a new member; when every pair reduces to zero the set is closed and reduction by it decides membership
requires: a well-founded order on leading terms
fails_when: intermediate expression swell; doubly exponential worst case

bit.name: reduce many pair combinations at once by row reduction of a shared matrix
bit.mechanism: instead of reducing one pair combination at a time, select a whole batch of pairs of the same size, write them and everything needed to reduce them as rows of one matrix over the monomials, row-reduce once, and add every new leading term that appears
requires: sparse linear algebra
fails_when: matrices can be huge; many rows reduce to zero (the F5 criterion avoids them)

bit.name: orient equations into rules and add the normal forms of critical overlaps as new rules
bit.mechanism: turn each equation into a rewrite rule pointing downhill in a termination order; wherever two rules' left sides overlap, rewrite the overlap both ways to normal forms; if the results differ, orient that pair as a new rule; repeat until no overlap yields a new rule, when rewriting decides equality
requires: a termination order that can orient every equation
fails_when: an unorientable equation halts the procedure; may run forever

bit.name: split by a gcd with a random element raised to half the group order
bit.mechanism: a product of equal-degree factors splits the residue ring into components; raise a random element to half the order of each component's multiplicative group, so it becomes plus or minus one in each component independently; the gcd of (result minus one) with the input collects exactly the components where it was plus one
requires: a squarefree input already separated by factor degree
an odd field size
fails_when: each trial splits with probability about one half; needs a separate handling in characteristic two

bit.name: solve for a rational certificate that telescopes the sum
bit.mechanism: write the term ratio as a quotient of polynomials in a normalised form, bound the degree of an unknown polynomial from that form, and solve the resulting linear system; a solution gives a closed form whose consecutive differences are the terms, and no solution proves that no such closed form exists
requires: a term ratio that is a rational function
fails_when: sums with no hypergeometric closed form return a proof of absence, not a value

bit.name: cancel the leading term with a multiple of a divisor, repeatedly
bit.mechanism: while some divisor's leading term divides the current leading term, subtract the matching multiple of that divisor and record it in the quotient; a leading term that no divisor divides is moved to the remainder; terms are taken in a fixed order so the process ends
requires: a term order in which leading terms decrease
fails_when: with several divisors the remainder depends on their order unless the set is closed

entry: Pollard's kangaroo algorithm (also known as Pollard's lambda algorithm)

bit.name: run a tame walk from a known point and a wild walk from the target, with value-determined jumps, until they meet
bit.mechanism: each walk jumps by an amount chosen from the current value alone, so once two walks land on a common point they coincide forever; start one from a known exponent, record its distance travelled, start the other from the unknown, and when the wild walk hits a point the tame one recorded, the two distances give the unknown
requires: the unknown known to lie in an interval
a jump function of the value alone
fails_when: the walks may miss; expected cost is the square root of the interval width

bit.name: guess the output size, run an output-sensitive procedure against it, and square the guess on failure
bit.mechanism: run a procedure whose cost depends on an assumed output size (here: hull the input in groups of that size, then wrap over the group hulls for that many steps); if the output is not finished within the guess, square the guess and start over; the doubling-of-exponents makes the total cost proportional to the final successful run
requires: an inner procedure whose cost is controlled by the guess
fails_when: the wasted runs are cheap only because the guess grows so fast

entry: Gift wrapping algorithm or Jarvis march

bit.name: repeatedly pick the point that makes the smallest turn from the current edge
bit.mechanism: start at an extreme point; among all remaining points choose the one such that every other point lies to one side of the line from the current point to it (the smallest angular turn), step to it, and repeat until the start is reached
requires: an orientation test on three points
fails_when: cost is points times hull size; slow when most points are on the hull

bit.name: sort by angle around a pivot, then pop any point that makes a non-left turn
bit.mechanism: sort the points by angle about the lowest point, walk them in that order pushing onto a stack, and whenever the top two stack points and the new point fail to turn left, pop the top; what remains on the stack is the hull in order
requires: an orientation test
a sort
fails_when: collinear points need a tie rule

bit.name: find the hull edge that bridges the median split, then recurse on each side
bit.mechanism: split the points by a vertical median line, find directly (by a prune-and-search over point pairs) the single hull edge that crosses the line, discard every point under that edge, and recurse on the two sides; the work is proportional to the input times the log of the output size
requires: linear-time median and a bridge-finding routine
fails_when: large constants; rarely faster in practice

bit.name: take the farthest point from the edge, discard the triangle's interior, and recurse on the two new edges
bit.mechanism: from a starting edge between two extreme points, find the point farthest from it; that point is on the hull; drop every point inside the triangle it forms, and recurse on the two edges from it; a random-like input gives linearithmic time
requires: a point-to-line distance
fails_when: quadratic when the points lie near a circle

bit.name: mark a point as surface if some cone from it contains no other point
bit.mechanism: for each point, test a set of cone directions of fixed opening angle; if any cone anchored at the point holds none of its neighbours, the point is on the surface; otherwise it is interior
requires: a cone opening angle and neighbour radius (policy)
fails_when: concave pockets fool the test; parameter-dependent

bit.name: propagate distances along each axis in turn
bit.mechanism: compute for every grid cell its distance to the nearest marked cell by handling one axis at a time: a pass along rows gives the nearest marked cell within each row, then a pass along columns combines those row results (as a lower envelope of parabolas) into true distances; each pass is linear
requires: a separable distance (sum of per-axis terms)
fails_when: non-separable metrics

bit.name: store every point in the frame of each basis pair, then vote at query time
bit.mechanism: offline, for every ordered pair of model points as a basis, express all other model points in that basis and store (quantised coordinates -> model, basis) in a table; online, pick a basis from the scene, express the scene points in it, look each up and vote; a model-basis pair with many votes is a match under the transformation
requires: a quantisation grid (policy)
a transformation group fixed by two points
fails_when: table size is cubic in model points; quantisation boundaries lose votes

bit.name: grow a simplex toward the origin using support points of the difference shape
bit.mechanism: the two shapes intersect exactly when their pointwise difference contains the origin; keep a small simplex of difference points, find the point of the difference shape farthest in the direction from the simplex toward the origin (one support query per shape), add it, drop the vertex that no longer helps, and repeat until the origin is enclosed or no progress is possible (the closest distance)
requires: a support function for each convex shape
fails_when: non-convex shapes must be decomposed; numerical stall near touching

bit.name: start at the nearest of a few random samples, then walk across neighbours toward the target
bit.mechanism: draw a handful of random cells, take the one whose reference point is closest to the query, and then step from cell to adjacent cell in the direction of the query until the query falls inside the current cell; no index is built
requires: adjacency between cells
a sample count (policy)
fails_when: non-convex regions can trap the walk

bit.name: move each vertex toward the mean of its neighbours
bit.mechanism: for every vertex compute the average position of its connected neighbours and move it there (or part of the way); repeat a few rounds; the mesh loses noise and small features shrink
requires: a connectivity graph over positions
fails_when: shrinkage; boundary vertices need fixing

bit.name: sweep a line across the plane and test only neighbours in the active order at each event
bit.mechanism: sort the segment endpoints as events; as a vertical line sweeps them, keep the segments it currently crosses in their vertical order; when a segment starts, ends, or two segments cross, only the segments that became adjacent in that order can newly intersect, so test just those and schedule any crossing found as a future event
requires: an ordered set for the active segments
a priority queue of events
fails_when: degenerate inputs (shared endpoints, vertical segments) need special rules

bit.name: rotate two parallel support lines around the hull, advancing whichever has the smaller angle to its next edge
bit.mechanism: rest two parallel lines on opposite vertices of a convex polygon; rotate both together, at each step turning by the smaller of the two angles needed to reach the next edge and advancing that vertex; every pair of opposite vertices is visited once, in one pass around the polygon
requires: a convex polygon in order
fails_when: parallel edges produce ties

bit.name: count the edge crossings of a ray from the point and read the parity
bit.mechanism: shoot a ray from the point in any fixed direction and count how many polygon edges it crosses; an odd count means inside, even means outside; the winding-number variant sums signed crossings instead
requires: a segment-ray intersection test
fails_when: a ray through a vertex needs a tie rule

bit.name: sum the signed cross products of consecutive vertices
bit.mechanism: walk the vertices in order, add each x times the next y and subtract each y times the next x, wrapping at the end; half the absolute total is the area and its sign gives the orientation
requires: vertices in boundary order
fails_when: self-intersecting polygons give signed cancellation

entry: Ruppert's algorithm (also known as Delaunay refinement)

bit.name: insert the circumcentre of each bad triangle until all meet the quality bound
bit.mechanism: while any triangle has an angle below the bound, insert its circumcentre as a new vertex and re-triangulate locally; if the new point would land too close to an input segment, split that segment at its midpoint instead; termination follows because inserted points are never closer than the local feature size allows
requires: an input with no very small angles between segments
a quality bound (policy)
fails_when: small input angles can prevent termination

bit.name: delete the triangles whose circumcircle contains the new point and refill the hole from it
bit.mechanism: start with a super-triangle; insert points one at a time: remove every triangle whose circumscribed circle contains the new point (they form a connected hole), and connect the new point to every edge of the hole boundary; the empty-circle property is restored after each insertion
requires: an in-circle test
a locating step for the containing triangle
fails_when: four co-circular points are ambiguous; worst case quadratic

bit.name: sweep a line while maintaining a front of parabolic arcs, handling site and circle events
bit.mechanism: as a line sweeps across the sites, maintain the curve of points equidistant from the line and the nearest site behind it (a chain of parabolic arcs); a new site splits an arc, and three consecutive arcs whose sites are co-circular predict a vertex where the middle arc vanishes; processing these two event types in order builds all cell boundaries
requires: an ordered structure for the arc front
a priority queue of events
fails_when: numerical fragility in the circle events

bit.name: grow a surface from a front edge, adding one triangle at a time
bit.mechanism: start from a seed triangle; keep the boundary edges as a front; for each front edge choose the nearby point that forms the best-shaped triangle satisfying a local empty-sphere test, add it, and update the front; stop when the front is empty
requires: a point cloud dense relative to surface curvature
a neighbour query
fails_when: holes where sampling is sparse; fronts can collide
